title: pr-1234-review-scratchpad-kv-cache-batching
content:
Context:
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1234 (kv-cache + batching refactor)
- Author: Priya Sharma
- Goal: unify KV cache lifecycle across multi-tenant pipelines and introduce batch-aware cache eviction to reduce cache thrash under mixed seq-len workloads.
- High-level: move KV ownership to RequestContext, add CacheShard abstraction, change batching selection to prefer same-shard sequences.

Quick notes / first pass impressions:
- Big wall of changes across cache/*, batching/*, and request_context.*. Need to be careful: ownership changes are risky for concurrency and SRE.
- Good: unit tests added for CacheShard put/get and simple eviction path.
- Missing: integration tests around multi-tenant simultaneous requests (different tenant ids) hitting same shard; potential cross-tenant leakage if keys collide.

Checklist (things to verify before approving):
- [ ] Correctness: no change in KV semantics for existing callers unless explicitly intended. Walk through RequestContext lifecycle in sync and async paths.
- [ ] Concurrency: ensure CacheShard uses proper locks or lock-free data structures when accessed by batching worker threads. Look for possible double-free on eviction path.
- [ ] Memory safety: any realloc/resizing of shard maps should be thread-safe. Check use of std::vector vs concurrent hash map.
- [ ] Tests: add integration test that simulates 50 concurrent short-seq + 50 long-seq requests to validate no cross-contamination and stable hit-rate.
- [ ] Telemetry: ensure metrics expose per-shard hit/miss rates and eviction counts. Add tags for tenant_id and model_variant.
- [ ] Backwards compatibility: ensure protobuf schema (if any) for cached keys unchanged.
- [ ] Performance: run microbench with existing workloads (batch size sweep 1..64, seq len 32/256) and compare p99 latency and token-throughput against main branch.
- [ ] Rollout plan: require canary on Dedicated cluster with 10% traffic for 24h before full rollout.
- [ ] Security: verify no logging of raw tokens on cache misses. PR touches logging in cache/evict.cpp - ensure sanitized.

Specific code comments / questions to leave on PR:
- cache/shard.h: line ~120 - why use a plain unordered_map here? Should we switch to tbb::concurrent_unordered_map or a read-optimized RW lock? Potential hotspot under high read concurrency.
  - Suggested: add comment about expected contention levels; consider per-bucket mutexes if simple solution preferred.

- request_context.cpp: lifecycle is mutated such that RequestContext::drop() is now called from batching worker - need to confirm this does not race with async callbacks in model_runner. Can we add an assert in debug build that validates no pending callbacks when context is dropped?

- batching/scheduler.cpp: batch selection now groups by shard id then by seq len. This is good for cache locality but might hurt latency for low-traffic shards (head-of-line blocking). Suggest adding a max-wait threshold override to allow single-shard small batches to be flushed early.

- cache/evict.cpp: eviction callback calls tenant_metrics->inc(); is tenant_metrics nullable? Add null-check or clarify ownership. Also big loop there could O(N) on eviction; consider amortized eviction or cap loop iterations per call.

Refactor ideas (follow-ups, not blockers):
- Introduce CacheMetricsAggregator that collects per-shard counters and emits aggregated summaries every 10s to reduce metric cardinality. Follow-up PR.
- Abstract ShardSelector behind a policy interface so we can experiment with LRU vs frequency-based eviction without touching scheduler.
- Consider storing short sequence KV entries in a separate fast-path structure (e.g., slab allocator) to avoid heap churn for tiny kvs. Might reduce GC/alloc pressure.

Tests to add (concrete):
- integration/test_kv_cache_multi_tenant.py: create 3 tenants, run interleaved requests, assert no cross-tenant hits and expected hit-rate after warmup.
- perf/benchmark_kv_cache.cc: benchmark get/put under different levels of concurrency and key sizes.
- unit/cache_shard_eviction_test.cpp: ensure eviction maintains invariants and no dangling pointers.

Follow-ups / TODOs (assignable):
- [ ] @Priya: add integration test and docs for RequestContext lifecycle changes. (blocking for merge)
- [ ] @Avery: run perf harness and paste numbers here + compare with baseline. (high priority)
- [ ] @Tae: review concurrency primitives and recommend replacement for unordered_map if needed.
- [ ] Add canary rollout steps to deploy runbook (ops playbook). Link to runbook template: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/Runtime+Rollout+Playbook

Open questions / uncertainties:
- Does the CacheShard keyspace include tenant_id prefix always? I saw in some callsites it's passed as "tenant:session:hash" and other callsites pass raw session id. Need to standardize.
- How does this interact with KV cache persistence (if any) on Dedicated nodes? PR mentions persistent snapshots but no implementation details.
- Are there any cross-region concerns if shard_ids are computed differently per-node? Might break routing if hash function changed.

Notes to self (random):
- Re-run unit tests locally with ASAN/TSAN after making concurrency comments. If TSAN flaps, prioritize fixing locks.
- If we require tbb dependency, check impact on binary size and distro packaging. Reach out to infra/package.

Suggested review PR checklist comment (short):
Thanks Priya — big change set, nice tests. A few concurrency and rollout concerns (see inline). Please add the multi-tenant integration test and a perf run before we merge. Also add metrics for per-shard hit/miss/eviction and confirm no raw-token logging. Once tests+perf done, recommend canary 10% for 24h.

End of scratchpad.

-- Jordan
